bug_semantics: CWE-400 on Authorino's HTTP metadata path keyed by AuthConfig/AuthPolicy sharedSecretRef. A Developer-persona policy names a Kubernetes Secret (loaded in full with no size cap) and an attacker-controlled URL; on every authorization request Authorino injects that secret as outbound credentials (default Authorization Bearer) and then json.Decoder.Decode / io.ReadAll the entire HTTP response with no byte limit. A large secret or a large metadata body exhausts the single Authorino instance so every AuthPolicy on the cluster stops evaluating. CVSS UI:R is the victim request that triggers the outbound call. Sibling CVE-2025-25207 is unbounded callback count; CVE-2025-25209 is one-line secret leakage over the same HTTP+sharedSecretRef channel.

reasoning: Vulnerability-first: CVE.org and Red Hat still publish this as a real CWE-400 in Authorino reached via AuthPolicy sharedSecretRef; GHSA withdrawn_at is not authoritative and is null anyway. The attack is a Developer AuthPolicy/AuthConfig HTTP metadata (or later HttpEndpointSpec callback/OPA) entry that references a Secret and a URL the attacker hosts. Authorino materializes the whole secret into the in-memory evaluator and, on each authz request, sends it as credentials then allocates the full response. That matches 'bring down the Authorino service, preventing the evaluation of all AuthPolicies' on a single instance. BIC is a85b10f, the first public write of sharedSecretRef plus the unbounded secret copy and HTTP body decode; the parent tree lacks those files/symbols. PR #100 is a merge with reconstructable members, so the merge itself is not the BIC. AI is judged only on that BIC commit object: human author/committer Guilherme Cassolato, GPG-signed, no AI trailers. Closed NOT_AI with unpatched because GHSA patched=None, Bugzilla NEW, and HEAD still has the unbounded ReadAll/Decode and uncapped secret load.

potential_fix.approach: Enforce a default (not operator-opt-in) maxResponseBytes via io.LimitReader before json.Decode/io.ReadAll in GenericHttp.Call and the other HttpEndpointSpec evaluators, and reject or truncate Secret values loaded from sharedSecretRef above a small credential-sized cap before injecting them into outbound headers/query/cookies.
potential_fix.rationale: The availability sink is unbounded allocation on the sharedSecretRef-authenticated outbound HTTP path. A mandatory response-body cap plus a secret-size cap stops a Developer-controlled AuthPolicy from OOMing the shared Authorino process. Open PR 672 is only a starting point because maxResponseBytes is omitted-unlimited.
